result.title: How Reliable Are Explanations of Language Models That Detect Insider Threats?
result.summary: Organizations monitor their workers' activity for insider threats, in which workers misuse their legitimate access, by copying confidential files before leaving. Detectors score how unusual each day of activity is, flagging the most unusual for an analyst to review. Prominent current approaches use opaque neural networks, so explanations of a flag point to internal features: patterns of neuron activity most active on days of misuse. We audit such explanations for language-model detectors trained on CERT's simulated workplace logs. To test an explanation, we see what happens to the detector's score when we remove its features inside the model. We compare this to a control: a change that is as similar as possible to the removal, but without actually removing the features. Because defining "similar" requires choosing a metric, our central contribution is the tipping radius: a first-order prediction of how far that metric must move before the difference between removal and control disappears, a measure of how fragile the result is to that choice. In 33 of 34 runs of seven language models, the tipping radius is at most 18% of the distance between two standard choices of metric. Moving that far removes at least 58% of the difference or reverses it, while random moves of the same size leave it largely intact. The result replicates in thirteen of fourteen pre-declared primary runs on openly released models, though on our trained detectors the difference is often too small to measure. We also find that a flag's score partly reflects who the worker is, not what they did, and that the features named depend on whom they are compared against. Audits should therefore fix the control's metric in advance, report its tipping radius, and disclose that comparison.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计基于语言模型的内部威胁检测器的解释可靠性：在模型内部移除被指认的神经元特征，并与「尽量相似但未真正移除」的对照比较，提出 tipping radius 来量化这一差异对相似性度量选择有多脆弱，并在 CERT 模拟办公日志上的七个模型、34 次运行中检验；还发现告警分数部分反映「是谁」而非「做了什么」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「移除 vs 匹配对照 + 度量脆弱半径」的审计思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容对答案的因果贡献是否只是归因度量的人为产物，与贡献分配和因果作用评估有概念联系；但对象为日志异常检测而非视觉推理，仅作启发。
